title: The Bicycle Bell
learning_objectives: Read independently and infer a character's motive from actions
Explain a misunderstanding and how it was cleared up
parent_prompts: Let the child read alone. After: why did Tim think Lan was cross? What was really going on?

pages.text: Tim's bicycle had a silver bell that went ting-a-ling. He rang it at dogs, at pigeons, and at his friend Lan every morning on the way to school. Lan always waved back.
pages.illustration_brief: Tim (red cap) on a bike ringing a bell; Lan waving from a gate.
pages.audio_script: Tim's bicycle had a silver bell that went ting-a-ling. He rang it at dogs, at pigeons, and at his friend Lan every morning on the way to school. Lan always waved back.
pages.image_alt: Tim on a bike ringing a bell; Lan waving from a gate.

pages.text: On Monday, Lan did not wave. She was looking at the ground. Tim rang the bell twice. Nothing.
pages.illustration_brief: Lan at the gate looking down; Tim on the bike, bell hand raised, puzzled.
pages.audio_script: On Monday, Lan did not wave. She was looking at the ground. Tim rang the bell twice. Nothing.
pages.image_alt: Lan at the gate looking down; Tim on the bike, bell hand raised, puzzled.

pages.text: On Tuesday, the same. Wednesday too. Tim stopped ringing. "She is cross with me," he decided. But he could not think what he had done.
pages.illustration_brief: Tim cycling past, not ringing, glancing back over his shoulder; Lan still looking down.
pages.audio_script: On Tuesday, the same. Wednesday too. Tim stopped ringing. She is cross with me, he decided. But he could not think what he had done.

vocabulary.example: Mum was cross when I spilled the juice.

pages.image_alt: Tim cycling past, not ringing, glancing back; Lan still looking down.

pages.text: On Thursday he got off the bike and walked it up to the gate. Lan was crouched down by the wall. In front of her, in a shoebox lined with a scarf, was a very small bird.
pages.illustration_brief: Lan crouched by a wall; a shoebox with a scarf and a tiny bird inside; Tim leaning the bike, looking over her shoulder.
pages.audio_script: On Thursday he got off the bike and walked it up to the gate. Lan was crouched down by the wall. In front of her, in a shoebox lined with a scarf, was a very small bird.
pages.image_alt: Lan crouched by a wall; a shoebox with a scarf and a tiny bird; Tim looking over her shoulder.

pages.text: "It fell out of the nest," Lan whispered. "I have been keeping it warm until Mum can take it to the vet. I did not wave because I did not want to scare it. And your bell..."
pages.illustration_brief: Close on the shoebox: a fledgling nestled in the scarf; Lan's finger to her lips.
pages.audio_script: It fell out of the nest, Lan whispered. I have been keeping it warm until Mum can take it to the vet. I did not wave because I did not want to scare it. And your bell.

vocabulary.example: She whispered a secret in my ear.

pages.image_alt: Close on the shoebox: a fledgling nestled in the scarf; Lan's finger to her lips.

pages.text: Tim looked at his silver bell. Ting-a-ling, every morning, right next to a frightened bird. His face went hot. "I thought you were cross," he said.
pages.illustration_brief: Tim looking at the bell on his handlebars, cheeks red.
pages.audio_script: Tim looked at his silver bell. Ting-a-ling, every morning, right next to a frightened bird. His face went hot. I thought you were cross, he said.
pages.image_alt: Tim looking at the bell on his handlebars, cheeks red.

pages.text: "Cross? No!" Lan almost laughed, then remembered and whispered it instead. "I just could not shout across the road."
pages.illustration_brief: Lan with a hand over her mouth, eyes smiling; Tim relieved.
pages.audio_script: Cross? No! Lan almost laughed, then remembered and whispered it instead. I just could not shout across the road.
pages.image_alt: Lan with a hand over her mouth, eyes smiling; Tim relieved.

pages.text: On Friday, Tim rode past the gate without a sound. Lan looked up and gave a tiny wave. The bird was gone to the vet, but the quiet stayed for one more day, just to be safe.
pages.illustration_brief: Tim gliding past silently; Lan giving a small wave; the empty shoebox by the wall.
pages.audio_script: On Friday, Tim rode past the gate without a sound. Lan looked up and gave a tiny wave. The bird was gone to the vet, but the quiet stayed for one more day, just to be safe.
pages.image_alt: Tim gliding past silently; Lan giving a small wave; the empty shoebox by the wall.

quiz.prompt: Why did Tim think Lan was cross?
quiz.explanation: Lan did not wave on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday (pages 2 and 3), so Tim decided she was cross.

quiz.prompt: Why did Lan really stop waving?

options.text: She did not want to scare the baby bird

quiz.explanation: Page 5: I did not wave because I did not want to scare it.

quiz.prompt: Why did Tim's face go hot?

options.text: He felt bad about ringing the bell near the frightened bird

quiz.explanation: Page 6: he thought of the bell ringing next to a frightened bird, and his face went hot. That is embarrassment.

options.text: In a shoebox lined with a scarf

quiz.explanation: Page 4: in a shoebox lined with a scarf, was a very small bird.

quiz.prompt: Tell a grown-up what Tim thought was happening, what was really happening, and how he found out.
quiz.rubric: not yet: says a bird; with support: Tim thought Lan was cross, with prompting; independent: thought she was cross because no wave, really she was protecting a fallen bird, he found out by walking up to the gate
quiz.explanation: Separating the wrong guess from the real reason shows the child followed the misunderstanding.

items.text: Tim finds the bird in the shoebox.

activities.prompt: Which page shows he was wrong?

prompts: Have you ever thought someone was cross when they were not?
What could Tim have done on Monday instead of guessing?

off_screen_prompt: Next time someone seems quiet, ask them one kind question before you guess why.
